Iritis (inflammation of the iris) is a component of the broader diagnosis of endophthalmitis, which involves inflammation of the entire eye's interior. The record describes an iris granuloma and fibrin in the anterior chamber, consistent with iritis, but the overall condition is more severe and widespread.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Iritis as a component of endophthalmitis

candidate_relations.reason: Uveitis is inflammation of the uvea (iris, ciliary body, choroid). Endophthalmitis is a severe form of intraocular inflammation that involves the vitreous and/or aqueous humor, often extending beyond just the uvea. The clinical findings (3+ cells with fibrin in the anterior chamber, hypopyon) are consistent with severe anterior uveitis, which is a component of endophthalmitis.
candidate_relations.scope_detail: Uveitis as a component of endophthalmitis
